deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a derivation. It is a draft table of contents ('Inhalt') for Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The numbers at the right of each item are page numbers of the manuscript. The previous page is the draft of the estimate belonging to Art. 16 of this list: the logarithmic lower bound for the Dirichlet integral in a thin strip, and the example (log 1/ρ)^α with α<1/2. Item by item, in modern terms:

(1) Definition. w=u+iv is a function of z=x+iy if dw/dz is independent of the direction of dz, i.e. complex differentiability. This is motivated by the remark that every function given by an analytic expression has this property.

(2) z and w are represented by points O and Q of two planes A and B. The dependence is viewed as a mapping (Abbildung) of one plane onto the other.

(3) If dw/dz is independent of dz, the map is similar in its smallest parts, i.e. conformal wherever w'≠0.

(4) Direction-independence is equivalent to the Cauchy–Riemann equations u_x=v_y, u_y=-v_x. From these follow Δu=0 and Δv=0.
  - [mine] u_xx = v_yx = v_xy = -u_yy; similarly for v.

(5) The plane A is replaced by a bounded surface T spread over A (a Riemann surface over the plane), with winding points (Windungspunkte, i.e. branch points).

(6) The connectivity (Zusammenhang) of a surface, using cross-cuts (Querschnitte).

(7) Gauss–Green theorem: ∫_T (∂X/∂x+∂Y/∂y) dT = −∫_{∂T} (X cos ξ + Y cos η) ds, for X, Y continuous on T. Here ξ, η are the angles of the inward normal, hence the minus sign.

(8) Local coordinates s (arc length along a curve) and p (normal distance) for the point O. Orientation is fixed by ∂x/∂s=∂y/∂p.

(9) Application of Art. 7 when X_x+Y_y=0 everywhere: the boundary integral vanishes, giving path-independence and conjugate functions.

(10) Conditions under which a solution u of Δu=0 (in general) is, with all its derivatives, finite and continuous in the interior of a surface T covering A. This is removability of singularities and regularity of harmonic functions.

(11) Properties of such a function: mean value, maximum principle, uniqueness.

(12) Conditions under which, inside a simply connected surface T covering A simply (schlicht), a function w of z is finite and continuous with all its derivatives.

(13) Discontinuities of such a function at an interior point: poles, isolated singularities, Laurent-type behaviour.

(14) Extension of Arts. 12–13 to interior points of an arbitrary planar surface, including branch points.

(15) Dirichlet principle. Ω(α,β)=∫_T [(α_x−β_y)^2+(α_y+β_x)^2] dT, under variation of α by functions λ that are continuous (or discontinuous only at isolated points) and vanish on the boundary.
  - Ω attains a minimum value always for some such function.
  - It does so for only one, once removable point discontinuities are excluded by alteration at single points.
  - [mine] Ω = D(α)+D(β) − 2∫(α_xβ_y−α_yβ_x) dT. The Jacobian term is a divergence and depends only on boundary data.

(16) Justification, by the 'Grenzenmethode' (limit method), of a proposition presupposed in Art. 15. This is the content of the previous page. A first version of item 16 is struck through.

(17) Existence theorem. T is a connected surface, cut by cross-cuts into a simply connected T*. If α+βi has finite Ω over T, it can be turned into a function of z in exactly one way by adding λ+μi, where:
  - (1) λ = 0 on the boundary, and μ is given at one point;
  - (2) λ in T and μ in T* are discontinuous only at isolated points, and only so mildly that the Dirichlet integrals of λ and μ stay finite;
  - the derivatives of μ agree on both sides of the cross-cuts.
  An unfinished reformulation of this item follows.

(18) Only the number and page 26 are written.

The red pencil at the foot ('Riemann bei Sanden(?)…') appears to be a later archival or provenance note.
errors: No mathematical errors. The sign in Art. 7 is correct for the inward-normal convention Riemann uses in the dissertation.

Art. 15 as first written claimed the minimum occurs for 'one and only one' function. Riemann deleted 'und nur für Eine' and added the qualification about removable discontinuities. This matches the modification derived on the previous page ('Es ist daher der Satz des vorigen Art. so zu modificiren').

Art. 15 asserts that the minimum is attained, i.e. the Dirichlet principle. This was later criticized by Weierstrass (1870) as unjustified in general and rigorously justified by Hilbert (1900/1904). Here it is stated, not proved.

results.what: Complex differentiability as direction-independence of dw/dz, with the Cauchy–Riemann equations and harmonicity of u and v
Holomorphic maps are similar in the smallest parts
Surface T spread over the plane with winding points; connectivity via cross-cuts
results.modern_name: Riemann surface (as a branched covering); connectivity / genus via cuts

results.what: Area integral of the divergence equals minus the boundary integral with the inward normal
Minimization of Ω=∫[(α_x−β_y)^2+(α_y+β_x)^2] under boundary-vanishing variations, with uniqueness up to removable point discontinuities
results.usually_credited_to: Green, Gauss, Thomson/Kelvin, Dirichlet; named by Riemann (1857); made rigorous by Hilbert

results.what: A function α+βi of finite Ω becomes holomorphic on a cut multiply connected surface after adding a unique correction λ+μi with stated boundary and single-valuedness conditions
results.modern_name: Riemann's existence theorem (dissertation Art. 18 form); Hodge-type decomposition

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft table of contents of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation and corresponds closely to its article structure. The only unpublished detail is the visible evolution of wording, e.g. the uniqueness clause in Art. 15. Historically interesting as a draft, but mathematically nothing new.

transcription_corrections: Art. 17: the interlinear insertion reads 'μ in einem Punkte gegeben' (λ is 0 on the boundary, μ is given at one point), not 'oder nur in einem Punkte gegeben'. Compare the published Art. 18: 'μ in einem Punkte beliebig gegeben'.

Art. 10: 'allenthalben' is inserted above 'einfach'. It is unclear from the image whether 'einfach' is actually struck; the sense intended is 'allenthalben einfach bedeckenden' or 'allenthalben bedeckenden'.

Art. 17 opening: the inserted replacement line reads 'Ist in einer beliebigen zusammenhängenden durch Querschnitte in eine einfach zusammenhängende {T*} zerlegten ebenen Fläche T eine Function α+βi von x, y gegeben, für welche ...'. The word 'gegeben' is added near 'α+βi von x, y'.
The red pencil note at the bottom is a later (non-Riemann) annotation; its reading 'bei Sanden Neuss' is uncertain.
